thread:
arjun: Heads-up — after the canary yesterday we saw a p95 token-latency regression on the continuous batching path, looks tied to microbatch window changes. profiling attached (small sample).
kelly: Ugh. Which param changed? microbatch interval or jitter?
mara: I rolled the coalesce delay down from 6ms -> 3ms to try to reduce tail for short sequences. That gave slightly better median but p95 moved ~+12%.
arjun: Interesting — do we have kernel-selection logs? smaller batches may force a fallback kernel that is slower for long sequences.
infra-bot: deploy 2026-03-14T20:03Z: canary rolled to 10% (sha: e3f4a1)
sam: I pulled traces. On hot paths when kv-cache hits are low the runtime is forming 1-2 token microbatches and triggering the generic matmul path. When kv-hit ratio > 0.8 we see expected fast kernel. When kv-hit ratio < 0.3 the slow path is used.
kelly: So reducing coalesce delay increased throughput of tiny requests but worsened mixing of seq lengths, causing more kernel mismatches?
arjun: Exactly. Also jitter reduction makes arrivals more synchronized, producing more same-time tiny batches, which get scheduled differently by the kernel selector. We need to tune three knobs together: microbatch_interval, coalesce_delay, and jitter_sigma.
mara: Proposal: run a factorial A/B on these ranges: microbatch_interval {2ms,5ms,10ms}, coalesce_delay {2ms,4ms,8ms}, jitter_sigma {0.5ms,2ms,6ms}. Measure p50/p95/p99 token latency, batch-size distribution, kernel-switch count, kv-hit ratio.
sam: Agree. Add token_budget_per_request as a fourth axis? We saw token budgets cause early flushes and artificially small batches. Maybe run token_budget {10,50,200} for chat endpoints.
kelly: Can we add a cheap profiler to increment a counter when kernel-switch happens per-request? then we can report kernel-switch rate in experiment.
arjun: Yes — I can add a lightweight counter metric (runtime.kernel_switch_count) and a histogram for batch_size_at_dispatch. low overhead.
infra-bot: perf-harness job queued: continuous-batch-experiment-180513; expected run 02:00Z
mara: Also watch KV cache staleness: if evictions are high we should see kv_hit drop and a correlated latency bump. I suspect one of the background compaction jobs coincided with canary.
sam: I replayed the canary traces — compaction spike at 20:01Z, eviction rate doubled. That lines up. So we need experiments with controlled eviction rates too.
arjun: Short-term mitigation: revert coalesce_delay to 6ms and increase jitter_sigma to 3ms to avoid synchronized tiny batches. That should reduce kernel-switch churn while we run the experiments.
kelly: sg, I'll push the revert and flag the canary.
mara: For the experiment sweep — can we tag runs with kernel build id so we don't confound with unrelated kernel changes?
arjun: Good call. Also pin model-quantization profile and runtime-kernel-version. We'll capture: batch_size_histogram, kernel_switch_count, kv_hit_ratio, p95_token_latency, and deploy_sha.
sam: I'll assemble a dashboard and add alerts on kernel_switch_count > 0.2 * requests.
kelly: Thanks. Action items: 1) arjun add kernel_switch metric, 2) infra schedule sweep, 3) mara revert coalesce_delay, 4) sam build dashboard.
arjun: I'll open PR for metric and set default microbatch_interval back to 5ms for the rolling canary.
kelly: thx — please paste the PR link here once up.
infra-bot: perf-harness started: continuous-batch-experiment-180513-run-1
kelly: looks like results coming in, will wait for p95 numbers and kernel_switch rates. :eyes:
